A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 30-page versions of the same work. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover all sections, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic preference-learning experiments, reward-model experiments on real preference datasets, and supplementary analyses in Section 7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the synthetic BT/non-BT comparison, real-dataset evaluations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The generative and discriminative BT objectives, model architectures, and connectivity-optimization procedures in Sections 5–7 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use identical synthetic scenarios and the same HH-RLHF, PKU-SafeRLHF, SHP, and UltraFeedback datasets. The introductory change from 'sport team ranking' to 'ranking' adds no evaluated task.

E2.justification: All evaluated comparisons are unchanged, including uniform-negative sampling versus connectivity-optimized sampling in Section 7.4. The newly cited ranking paper is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D retain identical sample sizes, model configurations, training and validation procedures, test distributions, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The small-margin subset analysis, connectivity sensitivity and optimization experiments, BT misspecification study, and appendix connectivity-estimator stability analysis are all unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed reporting with standard errors and the Appendix D.2 stability analysis using ten estimations per alpha aggregated across five seeds. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–4 contain identical values and curves. Their corresponding findings, including BT/non-BT errors and real-dataset accuracy rankings, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, and proofs remain identical, including Appendices A–C, the generalized connectivity result in Appendix D.3, and the perturbation derivation in Appendix D.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding discussion retain the same claims about CPRD, BT representability, KL projection, and the roles of margin and connectivity.

C2.justification: The interpretations of connectivity, margin, domain mismatch, and misspecification are unchanged. Section 8 retains the same practical limitations concerning unknown target scores, data curation, and conditional-independence testing.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures in Section 7 and Appendix D are unchanged, including architectures, optimizer settings, sampling procedures, and connectivity estimation. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Balcan et al. (2008), 'Robust reductions from ranking to classification,' to the introduction and bibliography. This modestly expands background attribution; the substantive related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 1 changes 'sport team ranking' to 'ranking' alongside the added citation, and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. The remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citation and reference cause local line wrapping on page 1 and bibliography reflow across pages 10–13. All figures and tables retain identical displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly expands background attribution through one ranking reference and a small introductory wording adjustment. The theoretical arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—are unchanged, and the accompanying reflow has no material effect on readability. These edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
